title: U.S. House · Texas's 37th District
area: A district covering most of Austin and Travis County.

context.text: Texas redrew its congressional map for the 2026 election cycle. Rep. Greg Casar, previously the incumbent for a differently drawn 35th District, is the incumbent for the redrawn 37th District under the new map. Rep. Lloyd Doggett, who had represented a 37th District, did not make the general-election ballot. Lauren Peña won the Republican primary runoff.

candidates.name: Greg Casar
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative (since 2023); Chair, Congressional Progressive Caucus

summary.text: Greg Casar is the incumbent U.S. Representative for the Austin-based 37th District. A former Austin City Council member, he chairs the Congressional Progressive Caucus and serves on the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform.

background.text: Born in Houston, Texas, in 1989; earned a bachelor's degree in political science from the University of Virginia.
Worked as policy director of the Workers Defense Project before his 2014 election to the Austin City Council.
Served on the Austin City Council, chairing its Planning and Neighborhoods Committee and serving as vice chair of the Public Safety Committee, before his 2022 election to Congress.

priorities.text: Chairs the Congressional Progressive Caucus after previously serving as its whip.

priorities.quote: It’s time for Congress to provide solutions for families and win truly universal and affordable child care for everyone.

priorities.text: Is a co-sponsor of the Green New Deal and similar clean-energy legislation.
priorities.quote: I’m a proud co-sponsor of the Green New Deal and similar legislation to create good union jobs in clean energy and protect communities harmed by pollution and natural disasters.

positions.summary: Supports achieving universal, affordable child care.
positions.quote: win truly universal and affordable child care for everyone

positions.summary: Co-sponsors the Green New Deal and related legislation to expand clean energy and address pollution.
positions.quote: I’m a proud co-sponsor of the Green New Deal and similar legislation to create good union jobs in clean energy and protect communities harmed by pollution and natural disasters.

positions.summary: Says Congress must ensure wealthy individuals pay a larger share in taxes to fund schools, roads, and community services.
positions.quote: Congress must ensure that the ultra rich pay their fair share in taxes and contribute to the schools, roads, and community services that we all use.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform and the House Committee on Education and Workforce in the 2025-2026 (119th) Congress.
Chairs the Congressional Progressive Caucus, after serving a term as its whip.

candidates.name: Lauren Peña
candidates.ballotNote: Won the Republican primary runoff against Ge'Nell Gary
candidates.currentRole: Legal advocate; founder, Peña Legal Advocacy

summary.text: Lauren Peña is an Austin-based legal advocate, founder of Peña Legal Advocacy, and self-described survivor of human trafficking who has testified before the Texas Legislature on welfare and housing policy.

background.text: Earned a bachelor's degree from Southern New Hampshire University in 2024, after attending the University of Texas and Austin Community College.
Founded and directs Peña Legal Advocacy, providing no-cost legal support across Texas.
Has been affiliated with the Austin Public Safety Commission, the Austin Community Police Review Commission, and the Travis County Republican Party.

priorities.text: Says welfare reform is her top priority, arguing the current system traps families in generational poverty.
priorities.quote: Welfare reform—long ignored by Republicans—is Lauren’s priority. The Democrat-run system traps families in generational poverty at taxpayers’ expense.

priorities.text: Says she supports law enforcement and favors building community trust through education and engagement rather than reduced police funding.

positions.summary: Opposes reducing police funding and says she supports law enforcement while working to build community trust.
positions.quote: Public Safety: Democrats defunded the police instead of educating the community.

sources.title: United States House of Representatives elections in Texas, 2026

researchNotes: Peña's Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey (completed in 2025) still refers to the seat by its former '35th Congressional District' number in places; that appears to reflect a pre-redistricting survey answer and was cross-checked against the current district-32 race listing on the Texas 2026 House elections overview.
